# Calibration inventory

Every question a console run can answer for the timing model (calibration #16), the kit ROM that measures it, and the spec rows and checks its answer closes. [hardware-run.md](hardware-run.md) is the procedure. A question's result is its `hw:<id>` check: pending:calibration-16 until `tools/n64-timing/calibration/ingest.py` stores a console capture, then pass when the console's values fall in the fork's range over its boot delays under the question's rule, fail otherwise. Kit ROMs: `kit-cpu`, `kit-vi`, `kit-dma`, `kit-hpos`, `kit-rdp`, `kit-span`, `kit-span2`, `kit-noise`, `kit-noise2`, `rdpstat-1prim`, `rdpstat-dpc`, `rdpstat-systemtest`, `rdpstat-unsynced`, `nemu64-timing`, `nemu64-cycle`, `nemu64-cop0hazard`, `kit-tex`, `kit-zmem`, `kit-zread`, `kit-cpu2`, `kit-bus`, `kit-vilb`, `cpu-llsc`, `kit-pif`. `ext:` names a ROM outside the repository that the procedure runs and ingestion stores; calibration/kit.py EXT_ROMS compares the ones with a reader. `none:` is a question with no kit ROM, with the reason.

## Coverage

Everything a console could have to decide: every behavior row (a fit, a model choice or an inference, and a reference a console run would confirm), checks with a failing, consistent-only or conditional result, rows that no corpus or only a report checks, and the hardware items of issues and follow-ups (tools/n64-timing/calibration/items.tsv). `behaviors.py --check` fails unless each one has a question or a reason in tools/n64-timing/calibration/undecidable.tsv: `not-hardware-decidable:` when no console run can decide it, `not decidable by this kit:` when a console could but this kit cannot, with what would. 227 entries: 210 with a question, 7 not hardware-decidable (no console run can decide them), 10 not decidable by this kit (a console could, with what the reason names).

| `vi.unfetched-sample` | model-choice; an inference in its reference or note; pending:report-only | not decidable by this kit: no cited fill order, model side waits on that capture. The CPU can read the VI's line buffer, the scaler's input, though not its output: n64brew Video_Interface rev 5791 documents VI_CTRL TEST_MODE (bit 7), KILL_WE (bit 11, which "possibly kills VI DMA writes to line buffers") and the test registers VI_TEST_ADDR (0x0440 0038) and VI_STAGED_DATA (0x0440 003C), but no source gives the order the VI fills the buffer or what the scaler reads for a sample past the fetched lines (MiSTer N64_MiSTer @5725381 rtl/VI.vhd keeps both test registers as plain storage, "usage unknown"). So pref 7 leaves the fork no model side for a kit question: the fork decodes VI words 0-13 only (ares/n64/vi/io.cpp) and reads 0 there. kit-vilb logs the buffer as a report (hardware-run.md, The VI line buffer). What would decide it: kit-vilb's console capture of the 128 line-buffer words at X_SCALE 0x201 and 0xE01 (16 bpp, AA_MODE replicate, Y_SCALE 0x800), which gives the fill order a line-buffer model would cite, and then a kit question against that model; or a video capture of the VI output for a mode that samples past the three fetched lines. MM never reaches it (cited inputs, inferred conclusion; no run counted unfetched samples): NTSC LAN1 runs Y_SCALE 1.0 and X_SCALE 0.5 over a 320-px line (decomp mm-decomp-60fps 56fa21dd0: src/boot/idle.c:107, src/libultra/vimodes/vimodentsclan1.c:11,17,24); the Bomber's Notebook hi-res mode sets Y_SCALE 2.0 but interlaced (src/code/z_vimode.c:81-84, src/code/sys_cfb.c:95), where VI::compose draws one row per output line from the line its fetch began at |

| `legacy.pif.boot-timeout` | legacy reference; pending:no-corpus | not decidable by this kit: the kit logs it as a report only. kit-pif never sends the PIF terminate-boot command (PIF RAM byte 0x3F bit 3, which every other kit ROM sends itself: romgen/runtime.py pif_terminate_boot) and logs COUNT every 10 ms over ISViewer until the PIF halts the CPU, from a cold boot through sc64deployer upload only (hardware-run.md, The PIF boot timeout). This is the terminate-boot timeout, not the PIF-CIC exchange, which n64brew PIF-NUS says runs as long as the console is powered and halts the CPU only on a failed or missing answer. The references differ: n64brew PIF-NUS says the PIF expects the command "before 5 seconds from boot" and halts the CPU if it does not come "within about 5 seconds from boot"; ares pif/hle.cpp starts 6 s at its WaitTerminateBoot state. COUNT counts from the IPL3's write of 0 (on the fork 1.8 ms before WaitTerminateBoot, measured), and no source bounds the offset from the PIF's timer start to COUNT's start, so the last COUNT cannot pick 5 s or 6 s. What would decide it: a cited bound on that offset under 0.5 s, half the 5 s to 6 s gap, which would allow a nearest-of-5-s-and-6-s rule on the last COUNT |

| `legacy.cart.eeprom-write` | legacy reference; pending:no-corpus | not decidable by this kit: the kit runs from a flashcart (docs/calibration/hardware-run.md:12-14: SC64 or ED64 X7), which takes the cartridge slot and serves the save device itself, so no kit ROM reaches a retail chip. Instrument limit: the SC64 stores an EEPROM write in its FPGA memory as the bytes arrive, with no write-busy time in the path (Polprzewodnikowy/SummerCart64 @a1e7996d fw/rtl/n64/n64_si.sv:347, 449-451), and the ED64 X7 emulates its save types and RTC with firmware whose timing is not published (krikzz/ed64-x-pub @cd2b91ef docs/rom_config_database.md:28-35, docs/real_time_clock.md:12-13; the repository has no FPGA source); a kit point at any resolution times the flashcart, not the chip. What would decide it: a retail cartridge carrying the real EEPROM with a timing ROM run on it (a cartridge with a modified ROM chip, or a dev cartridge with the chip) |
| `legacy.cart.rtc-tick` | legacy reference; pending:no-corpus | not decidable by this kit: the kit runs from a flashcart (docs/calibration/hardware-run.md:12-14: SC64 or ED64 X7), which takes the cartridge slot and serves the save device itself, so no kit ROM reaches a retail chip. Instrument limit: the SC64 reloads its Joybus RTC registers from its own I2C clock every 500 ms (Polprzewodnikowy/SummerCart64 @a1e7996d sw/controller/src/rtc.c:31, 458-461), so a kit point sees the flashcart's clock at a 500 ms grain against the row's 1 s tick, and the ED64 X7 emulates its save types and RTC with firmware whose timing is not published (krikzz/ed64-x-pub @cd2b91ef docs/rom_config_database.md:28-35, docs/real_time_clock.md:12-13; the repository has no FPGA source). What would decide it: the RTC chip itself, on an Animal Forest cartridge or a dev cartridge with the chip, running a timing ROM |

Both SC64 delays apply only when full_emulation is on (save type other than FLASHRAM_FAKE; flashram.c:70). A kit point at any resolution times the flashcart, not the chip.
